marks.gloss_en: ותרד בת פרעה לרחוץ, ואמר רבי יוחנן: שירדה לרחוץ מגילולי בית אביה -- the ground for calling her 'the Judean'
why is she called 'the Judean'? because she repudiated idolatry, as written 'and Pharaoh's daughter went down to bathe at the river' (Ex 2:5)
לעולם מבנימין קאתי ... על שום שכפר בעבודה זרה (= p_kafar_bead)
R' Yochanan: he actually came from Benjamin; why is he called Yehudi? because he repudiated idolatry
ילדה? והא רבויי רביתיה! -- Bitya did not bear Moses, she raised him
לומר לך שכל המגדל יתום ויתומה ... כאילו ילדו (= p_megadel_yatom)
to tell you that whoever raises an orphan boy or girl in his home, Scripture considers it as if he bore him
וכי מרד שמו? והלא כלב שמו! -- was his name Mered? was it not Calev?
אמר הקב"ה: יבא כלב שמרד ... וישא את בת פרעה שמרדה (= p_calev_mered)
the verse: 'and these are the sons of Bitya whom Mered took' -- object of the difficulty וכי מרד שמו
[Congregation of Israel:] that David did not kill Shimi, from whom was born Mordechai against whom Haman was jealous; and that Saul did not kill Agag, from whom was born Haman who afflicted Israel
R' Shimon ben Pazi, when he opened [expounding] Chronicles, said: all Your words are one, and we know how to expound them
Yered is Moses; why is he called Yered? for manna came down (yarad) for Israel in his days
'father... father... father' -- a father in Torah, a father in wisdom, a father in prophecy
'who had been exiled from Jerusalem' (Esth 2:6): Rava -- he went into exile of his own accord
תניא, רבי יהודה אומר: אנפקינון -- שמן זית שלא הביא שליש -- as Rav Huna
what is 'oil of myrrh' (Esth 2:12)? R' Chiya bar Abba: stacte
קרי לה הדסה וקרי לה אסתר? -- she is called both Hadassa and Esther
תניא: R' Meir, R' Yehuda, R' Nechemya on which was her name and why the other (= p_esther_shmah, p_hadassa_shmah_yehuda, p_hadassa_shmah_nechemya)
the verse: 'and he raised Hadassa, that is Esther' (Esth 2:7) -- she is called both Hadassa and Esther
R' Yehuda: her name was Hadassa; she was called Esther because she concealed (mesateret) her words
R' Nechemya: her name was Hadassa; she was called Esther because the nations called her after Istahar [the moon/Venus]
the verse: 'for she had neither father nor mother... and when her father and mother died' (Esth 2:7) -- the second clause is the object of למה לי
a tanna in R' Meir's name: do not read 'for a daughter' (levat) but 'for a house' (levayit) [i.e. a wife]
'the seven maidens' (Esth 2:9): Rava -- she counted the days of the week by them
Shmuel: he fed her pigs' necks
R' Yochanan: legumes
'in the evening she came and in the morning she returned' (Esth 2:14): R' Yochanan -- from that wicked one's disgrace we learned his praise: he did not have relations by day
'and Esther found favour' (Esth 2:15): R' Elazar -- this teaches that to each one she seemed to be of his own nation
'more than all the women... more than all the virgins' (Esth 2:17): Rav -- if he wished to taste a virgin's taste, he tasted it; a non-virgin's, he tasted it
'and the king made a great feast' (Esth 2:18): he made a feast and she did not reveal [her origin] to him; he lowered taxes and she did not reveal; he sent gifts and she did not reveal
[Mordechai's counsel, as the stam narrates:] a woman is jealous only of another woman's thigh
